title: Grusch colleague finds radar data on Big Sur

tellings.quote: someone told me that Dave grush was aware of the film and when he was on the task force he had a colleague check a military archive to see if they could find any confirmation of the Big Sir incident according to Dave this person did indeed find radar data confirming that an anomalous aerial object paced the Warhead

plain: The claim is that radar data in a military archive confirms the Big Sur incident, a 1964 missile test in California in which a film is said to show an unknown flying object pacing the warhead. Michels says someone told him that David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer who has said the US holds crashed non-human craft, knew of the film and, while serving on a Pentagon task force studying unexplained aerial sightings, had a colleague search the archive. According to what Michels was told, Grusch says the colleague found radar data showing an anomalous object paced the warhead, which, if true, would back the film with hard military records.
